finding: Walnut Creek says the 2025 California codes apply to every building permit application received on or after January 1, 2026, so an October 2026 submittal falls under the 2025 code cycle.
value: Published July 1, 2025; applies to applications on/after Jan 1, 2026
source_title: Building codes | City of Walnut Creek
quote: The 2025 Codes were published on July 1, 2025 and became applicable to all building permit applications made on or after January 1, 2026.

finding: The 2025 CBC that Walnut Creek enforces is based on the 2024 IBC with California amendments, and the city's municipal code amendments also apply.
source_title: Building codes | City of Walnut Creek
quote: 2025 California Building Code (Based on the International Building Code, 2024 Edition with State amendments)

finding: The permit application date decides which code edition applies, so a 2024 design must be checked against the 2025 codes if it is submitted now.
source_title: Multifamily Residential and Commercial Buildings | City of Walnut Creek
quote: The permit application date determines which codes are in effect for the project. Only those building codes that are in effect at the time of application will apply to the project.

finding: The Building Standards Commission publishes a summary of the 2025 Title 24 changes, which confirms the July 1, 2025 publication date and the January 1, 2026 effective date.
source_title: 2025 Title 24 California Code Changes (DGS/BSC)
quote: A summary of California amendments in the 2025 edition of Title 24, published July 1, 2025, and effective January 1, 2026

finding: Under CBC 2406.4.1, glass in any panel of a swinging door is a hazardous location, so the new 7'-0" x 8'-0" glass entry pair needs safety glazing.
value: CBC 2406.4.1: all glazing in swinging doors = hazardous location
source_title: Chapter 24 Glass and Glazing: California Building Code 2025 | UpCodes
quote: Glazing in all fixed and operable panels of swinging, sliding and bifold doors shall be considered to be a hazardous location.

finding: Under CBC 2406.4.2, the fixed sidelights are hazardous locations if their nearest edge is within a 24-inch arc of the door and their bottom edge is below 60 inches.
value: CBC 2406.4.2: within 24-in arc of door edge and bottom edge <60 in above walking surface
source_title: Chapter 24 Glass and Glazing: California Building Code 2025 | UpCodes
quote: the nearest vertical edge of the glazing is within a 24-inch (610 mm) arc of either vertical edge of the door in a closed position and where the bottom exposed edge of the glazing is less than 60 inches (1524 mm) above the walking surface shall be considered to be a hazardous location

finding: Safety-glazing rules cover each pane of a multipane assembly, so both lites of the double-pane units in hazardous locations must be safety glass.
value: CBC 2406.1: applies to panes in multipane glass assemblies
source_title: Chapter 24 Glass and Glazing: California Building Code 2025 | UpCodes
quote: Glazed areas in hazardous locations as defined in Section 2406.4, including glass mirrors, single panes of glass, laminated glass and panes in multipane glass assemblies, shall comply with Sections 2406.1.1 through 2406.1.4.

finding: Glass above the pony walls is a window hazardous location only if all four tests are met (pane over 9 sf, bottom edge under 18 in, top edge over 36 in, walking surface within 36 in); this wording comes from a Burbank plan-check list that cites CBC 2406.4.3 and should be confirmed against the 2025 text.
value: >9 sf; bottom <18 in; top >36 in; walking surface within 36 in
source_title: Burbank commercial correction list (Glass and Glazing, CBC 2406.4.3)
quote: a. The exposed area of an individual pane is greater than 9 square feet b. The bottom edge of the glazing is less than 18 inches above the floor c. The top edge of the glazing is greater than 36 inches above the floor d. One or more walking surfaces are within 36 inches

finding: Under 11B-404.2.2, at least one active leaf of the new double entry door must meet the clear-width and maneuvering-clearance rules.
source_title: 11B-404.2 Manual doors, doorways, and manual gates (2025 CBC) | Corada
quote: At least one of the active leaves of doorways with two leaves shall comply with Sections 11B-404.2.3 and 11B-404.2.4.

finding: Each door opening must give at least 32 inches of clear width, measured with the door open 90 degrees.
source_title: 11B-404.2 Manual doors, doorways, and manual gates (2025 CBC) | Corada
quote: Door openings shall provide a clear width of 32 inches (813 mm) minimum. Clear openings of doorways with swinging doors shall be measured between the face of the door and the stop, with the door open 90 degrees.

finding: Maneuvering clearances follow Table 11B-404.2.4.1 (front approach, pull side: 60 in perpendicular and 18 in beyond the latch); California adds 6 inches on the exterior side of exterior doors.
value: Front/pull: 60 in x 18 in beyond latch (+6 in exterior side); Front/push: 48 in (+12 in beyond latch if closer and latch)
source_title: 11B-404.2 Manual doors, doorways, and manual gates (2025 CBC) | Corada
quote: 5.  Add 6 inches (152 mm) at exterior side of exterior doors.

finding: The new 4-inch slab must be flat (no slope over 1:48 and no level changes) inside the door maneuvering clearances, except at compliant thresholds.
source_title: 11B-404.2 Manual doors, doorways, and manual gates (2025 CBC) | Corada
quote: Floor or ground surface within required maneuvering clearances shall comply with Section 11B-302. Changes in level, slopes exceeding 1:48, and detectable warnings shall not be permitted.

finding: Thresholds at the new entry door may be no more than 1/2 inch high; the CBC has no 3/4-inch beveled exception for existing or altered thresholds.
source_title: 11B-404.2 Manual doors, doorways, and manual gates (2025 CBC) | Corada
quote: Thresholds, if provided at doorways, shall be ½ inch (12.7 mm) high maximum. Raised thresholds and changes in level at doorways shall comply with Sections 11B-302 and 11B-303.

finding: Hinged doors in series need at least 48 inches between them plus the width of any door swinging into the space; with a 5'-2" (62 in) deep vestibule, an outer leaf of about 42 in that swings in would need about 90 in, so the outer pair would have to swing out (this is an inference from the stated dimensions).
value: 48 in min + width of doors swinging into space (11B-404.2.6)
source_title: 11B-404.2 Manual doors, doorways, and manual gates (2025 CBC) | Corada
quote: The distance between two hinged or pivoted doors in series and gates in series shall be 48 inches (1219 mm) minimum plus the width of doors or gates swinging into the space.

finding: California limits the opening force of exterior hinged doors to 5 pounds, which is hard to meet at a large glass pair without a powered leaf; the exception allows 8.5 lb on other leaves when one in eight leaves is powered.
source_title: 11B-404.2 Manual doors, doorways, and manual gates (2025 CBC) | Corada
quote: Exterior hinged doors: 5 pounds (22.2 N) maximum.

finding: Door hardware on the new entry pair must be mounted between 34 and 44 inches above the finish floor.
source_title: 11B-404.2 Manual doors, doorways, and manual gates (2025 CBC) | Corada
quote: Operable parts of such hardware shall be 34 inches (864 mm) minimum and 44 inches (1118 mm) maximum above the finish floor or ground.

finding: Swinging doors need a 10-inch smooth bottom surface on the push side, but stileless tempered glass doors with a tapered bottom rail are exempt from that height rule.
value: 10 in smooth surface; Exception 2 for tempered glass doors without stiles (11B-404.2.10)
source_title: 11B-404.2 Manual doors, doorways, and manual gates (2025 CBC) | Corada
quote: Tempered glass doors without stiles and having a bottom rail or shoe with the top leading edge tapered at 60 degrees minimum from the horizontal shall not be required to meet the 10 inch (254 mm) bottom smooth surface height requirement.

finding: Glazed doors and sidelights next to doors must have at least one glazed panel whose bottom is no higher than 43 inches above the floor.
value: 43 in max to bottom of glazing (11B-404.2.11)
source_title: 11B-404.2 Manual doors, doorways, and manual gates (2025 CBC) | Corada
quote: Doors, gates, and side lights adjacent to doors or gates, containing one or more glazing panels that permit viewing through the panels shall have the bottom of at least one glazed panel located 43 inches (1092 mm) maximum above the finish floor.

finding: Under 11B-202.4, any alteration triggers an accessible path of travel to the altered area, starting with a primary entrance, then toilets, drinking fountains, phones and signs.
source_title: 11B-202.4 Path of travel requirements in alterations, additions and structural repairs (2025 CBC) | Corada
quote: When alterations or additions are made to existing buildings or facilities, an accessible path of travel to the specific area of alteration or addition shall be provided. The primary accessible path of travel shall include:

finding: Under Exception 8, if the adjusted construction cost is at or below the valuation threshold, required path-of-travel upgrades are capped at 20 percent of that cost.
source_title: 11B-202.4 Path of travel requirements in alterations, additions and structural repairs (2025 CBC) | Corada
quote: When the adjusted construction cost, as defined, is less than or equal to the current valuation threshold, as defined, the cost of compliance with Section 11B-202.4 shall be limited to 20 percent of the adjusted construction cost of alterations, structural repairs or additions.

finding: The 2026 valuation threshold used for Exception 8 is $209,208, and DSA applies it to projects submitted after January 19, 2026.
source_title: Valuation Threshold Update for 2026 (Division of the State Architect)
quote: The 2026 Valuation Threshold is $209,208.00. It will be updated again in January 2027. Projects submitted to DSA after January 19, 2026 shall use this revised Valuation Threshold
source_date: Jan 2026; government-index excerpt (live page returned 404 when opened Oct 2026)

finding: UC Berkeley's access office confirms the same 2026 threshold of $209,208.00 and says it will be updated in January 2027.
source_title: Valuation Threshold | Disability Access & Compliance (UC Berkeley)
quote: DSA Valuation Threshold for 2026: $209,208.00

finding: DSA's history table shows the threshold was $203,611 in 2025 and $209,208 in 2026, so a 2025 figure appearing on some consultant pages is out of date.
source_title: Access Compliance Reference Materials (DSA)
quote: Year: 2026 | ENR Construction Cost Index (Jan.): 14109.11 | Valuation Threshold: $209,208.00 | Year: 2025 | ENR Construction Cost Index (Jan.): 13731.61 | Valuation Threshold: $203,611.00

finding: When path-of-travel spending is capped, an accessible entrance is the first priority, followed by an accessible route and then restrooms.
source_title: Valuation Threshold | Disability Access & Compliance (UC Berkeley)
quote: In choosing which accessible elements to provide, priority should be given to those elements that will provide the greatest access in the following order:

finding: Walnut Creek's commercial alteration bulletin requires full disabled-access plans and a plot plan showing accessible parking and the path of travel to the remodel area.
value: Required drawings: accessible parking + path of travel; complete disabled access plans
source_title: Information Bulletin IB-012: Submittal Requirements for Commercial Alterations (City of Walnut Creek)
quote: Accessible parking location and path of travel to area of remodel.  References to blow-up details for these items

finding: An Energy Code alteration is any change to a regulated component, including the envelope, so new storefront glazing is regulated only if it forms part of the conditioned envelope.
source_title: Energy Code Support Center: 2025 Nonresidential FAQ (CEC)
quote: An alteration is any change to a component that is regulated by the Energy Code, including water-heating system, ventilation system, space-conditioning system, indoor, outdoor, and sign lighting, electrical power distribution system, envelope, and any covered process.

finding: The 2025 NRCC-ENV-E envelope form says the daylighting rule for large high-ceiling spaces is the only prescriptive envelope requirement that applies to unconditioned spaces, which suggests unconditioned vestibule glazing has no fenestration U-factor or SHGC requirement.
value: Only prescriptive requirement for unconditioned spaces = daylighting (Section 140.3(c)), spaces >5,000 sf with >15 ft ceilings
source_title: 2025 NRCC-ENV-E Envelope Component Approach (CEC)
quote: Compliance with §140.3(c)/§170.2(b) is documented in Table L. This is the only prescriptive requirement which applies to unconditioned spaces.

finding: New for 2025, Section 120.7(e) requires vestibules at public entrances to spaces of 3,000 sf or more, but only for newly constructed buildings, so it should not apply to this existing 3,727 sf store; confirm with the building official.
value: Section 120.7(e); spaces ≥3,000 sf; newly constructed A, B, E, I, M
source_title: 2025 Energy Code Overview (CEC)
quote: Vestibules § 120.7(e) – adds mandatory requirements for vestibules at public entrances 2 that open into spaces 3,000 ft or more for newly constructed occupancy of assembly, business, education, institutional, and mercantile
source_date: June 2025 (government-index excerpt; the PDF redirected when opened)

finding: The 2025 code adds a mandatory 0.58 maximum U-factor when more than 150 sf of vertical fenestration is replaced; this would matter only if the new glazing were treated as conditioned envelope.
source_title: 2025 Energy Code Overview (CEC)
quote: § 141.0(b)1E – adds mandatory U-factor 0.58 for vertical fenestration 2 replacements over 150 ft

finding: A space counts as indirectly conditioned (and so regulated) if its heat-transfer area to the conditioned store exceeds its heat-transfer area to outdoors; the vestibule's unconditioned status therefore depends on the existing storefront wall and doors staying in place as the separation.
value: Indirectly conditioned = UA to conditioned space > UA to outdoors
source_title: 2022 Energy Code Fact Sheet: Single-Family Envelopes (City of Escondido)
quote: Conditioned Space, Indirectly is enclosed space that (1) is not directly conditioned space; and (2) either (a) has a thermal transmittance area product (UA) to directly conditioned space exceeding that to the outdoors or to unconditioned space

finding: CEC compliance-manual guidance (shown here with the residential sunspace example) says envelope requirements do not apply to an enclosed space that is neither directly nor indirectly conditioned.
value: Unconditioned space: envelope and mechanical requirements do not apply
source_title: 2025 Single-Family Compliance Manual Chapter 9 (CEC)
quote: The mechanical and envelope requirements of the Energy Code do not apply if the space is not directly or indirectly conditioned, which is demonstrated by the air and thermal barrier between the added sunspace and the existing conditioned space.

finding: Walnut Creek requires Design Review for all exterior remodeling of commercial buildings, completed before the building permit application, though the two reviews can sometimes run concurrently.
value: Design Review required before building permit
source_title: Information Bulletin IB-012: Submittal Requirements for Commercial Alterations (City of Walnut Creek)
quote: Design Review is required for all exterior remodeling of commercial buildings. Contact the Planning Division for Design Review information.

finding: All non-residential projects go through Discretionary Design Review, and small staff-delegated projects can take only a few weeks.
value: Discretionary Design Review; small projects: a few weeks
source_title: Design Review | City of Walnut Creek
quote: Only a few weeks may be required for small, staff delegated projects. Many months may be required for complex projects requiring an Environmental Impact Report.

finding: After a Design Review submittal, the applicant gets a Notice of Application Status with completeness and agency comments within 30 days.
value: 30 days to Notice of Application Status
source_title: Design Review | City of Walnut Creek
quote: After submittal, a planner will be assigned to your project. Within 30 days after the submittal, you will get a Notice of Application Status.

finding: Walnut Creek accepts permit applications only through its online portal; paper and emailed applications are no longer accepted.
source_title: Building Permits | City of Walnut Creek
quote: The City of Walnut Creek has fully committed to an all-online permitting system – all permit types shall be applied for via our Online Permit Portal. We are no longer accepting paper or emailed permit applications.

finding: The Building Division can be reached at 925-943-5834 or BuildingTech@walnutcreekca.gov, and the Duty Planner (for Design Review) at 925-256-3558 or DutyPlanner@walnut-creek.org.
source_title: Building Permits | City of Walnut Creek
quote: Please call 925-943-5834 for general questions and help, you may need to leave a voicemail.

finding: The city's target maximum for a commercial alteration is 18 business days for first review and 13 for rechecks, assuming Design Review is already complete.
source_title: Policy Bulletin PB-031: Plan Review Turnaround Times (City of Walnut Creek)
quote: | Commercial (multifamily residential and non-residential) | Alterations | 5 | 15 | 10 | 10 | - | 18 | 18 | 10 | 10 | 5 | - | 13 | 13 |

finding: Every commercial alteration needs fire approval, with plans submitted separately to the Contra Costa County fire district.
value: Fire approval required; 2 plan sets to the fire district
source_title: Information Bulletin IB-012: Submittal Requirements for Commercial Alterations (City of Walnut Creek)
quote: Please note that Fire approval is required for all commercial alterations.

finding: Because the building dates from 1957, the owner must have it evaluated for PCB and mercury materials and sign a self-certification before the tenant-improvement permit can be issued.
value: Applies to structures built or remodeled 1950–1980
source_title: Information Bulletin IB-012: Submittal Requirements for Commercial Alterations (City of Walnut Creek)
quote: Tenant Improvements and Commercial Demolitions where the structure was constructed or remodeled between 1950 and 1980 with building materials with PCBs concentrations of 50 ppm or greater

finding: In the FY2026–27 fee schedule, the building plan review fee equals 100 percent of the building permit fee.
value: Plan review = 100% of building permit fee
source_title: Master Fee Schedule FY2026 & FY2027 (City of Walnut Creek)
quote: A Building Plan Review Fee shall be 100 percent of the Building Permit Fee, as shown in the applicable fee resolu tion adopted by the City Council.

finding: Design review in the 'Small Additions/Remodel & Storefronts' category is billed at $231.12 per hour in FY2026, rising to $240.36 in FY2027.
source_title: Master Fee Schedule FY2026 & FY2027 (City of Walnut Creek)
quote: SmallAdditions/Remodel & Storefronts | per hour | 231.12 | 240.36

finding: Discretionary review deposits start at about $1,200 for a simple remodel, are drawn down hourly and are not a cap; building plan review switches to hourly billing after the third round.
value: Deposit from $1,200; hourly after 3rd plan-review round
source_title: Fees, rates, and deposits | City of Walnut Creek
quote: Deposits can range from $1,200 for a simple remodel to more than $10,000 for large development projects.

finding: A Bay Area glazier's 2025 guide puts fully installed commercial storefront systems at $50 to $150 per square foot.
source_title: How Much Do Storefront Windows Cost? Complete Price Guide | Insight Glass
quote: Materials alone run $25 to $75 per square foot, depending on glass specifications and frame quality. Fully installed costs, including labor, range from $50 to $150 per square foot.

finding: The same Bay Area guide prices double-pane insulated glass units at $35 to $60 or more per square foot and tempered glass at $18 to $30 per square foot.
source_title: How Much Do Storefront Windows Cost? Complete Price Guide | Insight Glass
quote: Insulated glass units (IGUs) with double-pane construction cost $35 to $60 per square foot or more.

finding: The Bay Area guide prices double glass entry door systems at $2,500 to $5,500 or more installed, including commercial hardware and closers.
source_title: How Much Do Storefront Windows Cost? Complete Price Guide | Insight Glass
quote: Double door entry systems with center mullions, panic hardware, or automatic openers run $2,500 to $5,500 or more.

finding: An Alabama glazier quotes $4,200 to $4,800 installed for a standard pair of aluminum storefront doors; this is a non-Bay Area national comparison, and Bay Area prices are likely higher.
source_title: Storefront Door Replacement Cost & Timeline | Sunbelt Glass
quote: $4,200-$4,800 installed

finding: A 2026 Bay Area guide puts installed stucco at $8 to $14 per square foot; this is a residential figure, and the small commercial pony walls will add framing and mobilization costs.
source_title: Stucco vs Siding 2026: Bay Area Cost and Performance Guide | Custom Home
quote: Stucco costs $8-$14 per square foot installed in the Bay Area and is the dominant exterior finish on homes throughout the region.

finding: A San Jose concrete contractor prices a broom-finished 4-inch slab at $10 to $16 per square foot installed in the Bay Area (about 194 sf here: 17'-0" plus 20'-9" bays x 5'-2"); small pours often carry minimum charges.
source_title: Concrete Patio Cost 2026: $10–$16/sq ft in the Bay Area | Dueling Trowels
quote: Broom finish, 4" slab$10–$16

finding: Walnut Creek requires commercial alteration plans to be stamped by a registered architect or engineer unless exempted by the Business and Professions Code, and the Building Official may waive this when no life-safety element is involved.
value: Architect or engineer stamp required unless B&P exemption
source_title: Information Bulletin IB-012: Submittal Requirements for Commercial Alterations (City of Walnut Creek)
quote: Plans must be signed and stamped by a registered architect or engineer, unless specifically exempted under the California Business and Professions Code.

finding: B&P Code 5537.5 exempts a civil engineer from the Architects Practice Act while practicing civil engineering, so a licensed P.E. (civil) may prepare and stamp plans for this alteration but may not use the title architect.
source_title: California Code, BPC 5537.5 (leginfo)
quote: A civil engineer authorized to use that title under the provisions of Chapter 7 (commencing with Section 6700), insofar as he or she practices the profession for which he or she is registered, is exempt from the provisions of this chapter

finding: B&P Code 6731 defines civil engineering to include preparing designs, plans and specifications for framed structures and buildings.
source_title: California Business and Professions Code § 6731 (leginfo)
quote: foundations, grading, framed and homogeneous structures, buildings, or bridges: (a) The economics of, the use and design of, materials of construction

finding: The California Architects Board's consumer guide states that civil engineers may design any building except hospitals and public schools.
value: Civil engineers: any building except hospitals/public schools
source_title: Consumer's Guide to Hiring an Architect (California Architects Board)
quote: Civil Engineers May design any building except hospitals and public schools.

finding: B&P Code 5538 lets anyone prepare plans for nonstructural storefronts, but this project replaces posts and adds a slab and walls (structural work), so the exemption likely does not cover it and a licensed stamp is needed.
value: B&P Code 5538(a): nonstructural or nonseismic storefronts only
source_title: California Code, BPC 5538 (leginfo)
quote: (a) For nonstructural or nonseismic storefronts, interior alterations or additions, fixtures, cabinetwork, furniture, or other appliances or equipment.

finding: B&P Code 6735 requires permitted civil engineering plans to carry the licensee's signature, seal and signing date on every sheet.
source_title: California Code, BPC 6735 (leginfo)
quote: All civil engineering plans and specifications that are permitted or that are to be released for construction shall bear the signature and seal or stamp of the licensee and the date of signing and sealing or stamping.

finding: P.E. licenses run two years from the assigned renewal date, and it is illegal to practice on an expired license, so a stamp showing expiration 6-30-25 must be checked for renewal before the plans are used.
value: 2-year validity; 60-day fee grace period only; no practice while expired
source_title: License Renewals | BPELSG
quote: You may not legally practice under an expired license. You must wait until BPELSG receives and processes the required payment for each license before resuming practice.

finding: Engineers now renew through BPELSG Connect (not BreEZe); a license unrenewed for five or more years cannot be renewed and requires a new application.
value: Renew via BPELSG Connect; 5-year delinquency limit
source_title: License Renewals | BPELSG
quote: A delinquent license may be reinstated by paying all accrued and unpaid renewal and delinquency fees. However, if your license has been delinquent for five (5) years or more, it cannot be renewed.

finding: Anyone can verify a P.E.'s status and expiration date through the board's License Lookup, which links to DCA Search (search.dca.ca.gov, BD=31); a 'Delinquent' status means no right to practice.
source_title: License Lookup | BPELSG
quote: Delinquent: The expiration date has passed, and the license has not been renewed. Delinquent licensees do not have the right to practice.

finding: Any contractor must be CSLB-licensed to bid on work of $500 or more, and the license can be verified free on cslb.ca.gov or at 800-321-2752.
source_title: What You Should Know Before Hiring a Contractor (CSLB)
quote: By law, anyone in California who contracts for or bids on a construction project valued at $500 or more (combined labor and material costs) must be licensed by the Contractors State License Board (CSLB).

finding: CSLB's Check a License tool searches by license number, business name or personnel name and shows license status and complaint disclosures.
source_title: Check A License | CSLB
quote: Look up a contractor license or Home Improvement Salesperson (HIS) registration to verify information, including complaint disclosure.

finding: The C-17 Glazing Contractor class covers fabricating and installing glass, frames, panels and doors, which matches the storefront glazing and the glass entry pair.
source_title: C-17 - Glazing Contractor | CSLB Licensing Classifications
quote: A glazing contractor selects, cuts, assembles and/or installs all makes and kinds of glass, glass work, mirrored glass, and glass substitute materials for glazing; executes the fabrication and glazing of frames, panels, sashes and doors; and/or installs these items in any structure.

finding: A B General Building contractor may take the prime contract because the job involves two or more unrelated trades (concrete, framing/stucco, glazing), and can subcontract the glazing to a C-17.
value: B&P 7057: B license; at least two unrelated trades
source_title: B - General Building Contractor | CSLB Licensing Classifications
quote: a general building contractor shall not take a prime contract for any project involving trades other than framing or carpentry unless the prime contract requires at least two unrelated building trades or crafts other than framing or carpentry
